blocks.x: DORA-grade resilience posture — third-party and incident evidence automated
A tier-1 US bank — Banking & Financial Services engagement delivered by a 12-person team over 9 months, US scope, commercial model: build-run (managed).

items: ICT third-party register spread across procurement spreadsheets; incident playbooks untested for years.
Evidence for resilience assessments assembled manually per audit; findings recurred without owners.
Board reporting on resilience was narrative, not measured.

blocks.x: We implemented the resilience program on Sentinel: the third-party register became a governed data product with tiering and exit evidence, incident playbooks moved to tested runbooks with two full exercises per year, and control tests ran continuously with failing-control workflows. The board pack now reports measured recovery times and coverage gaps.
The engagement was built to be handed over: named pod, runbooks in writing, operators enabled, and a Compound phase running challenger programs and conformance monitoring after the exit.

items: The committed move on this metric: 24%, measured against the baseline signed in week two
A global gaming studio (live-service title, 15M MAU)
The engagement is documented on its case page — what was measured, what moved and how the evidence was gathered.

blocks.x: Towers: Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust, Cloud, Edge & Platform Engineering. Platforms: Tele Medicine Platform, Driisti Smart Vision Glasses.

items: What moved unchanged between sectors, and why it was safe to move — stated plainly.
What does not transfer between estates, and the adaptation it needs — named before the pilot, not after.

blocks.x: Confidentiality note: the engagement runs under a name-withheld agreement. Reported metrics reconcile to the locked Diagnose baseline, and the method travels with the reference call.
